headline: Workflow and reference tooling for microbial species typing, profiling and genome comparison
label: Microbial Genomics Workflow Tooling
summary: New workflows target species assignment, nanopore 16S interoperability, SNP transmission clustering and MGnify v6 amplicon, viral and mobilome analyses.
synthesis: The dominant thread is packaging microbial identification and comparison methods into reproducible, accessible tooling. For species designation, Robust Cluster Typing uses ribosomal proteins in a Snakemake/Python workflow to assign genomes to species-level clusters, shown on Campylobacter. RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies sequenced variable regions for species-level identification. VPHYL converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects with HTML reports. SNP2Cluster-Py offers pathogen-agnostic, context-aware core SNP and transmission-cluster analysis, tested on Klebsiella and pneumococcal WGS. At resource scale, MGnify v6 adds amplicon variant analysis, expanded viral and mobilome annotation, Nextflow/Prefect automation and improved programmatic access. Deployment and genome comparison are addressed by Sparrowhawk, a WebAssembly framework for local, private browser tools, and nf-core/pairgenomealign, a Nextflow wrapper for LAST pairwise whole-genome alignment. Scopes differ; no cross-tool performance comparisons are reported.
